page: Amazon Web Services m4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.4 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration allocates 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU includes 45 MB of L3 cache, along with support for AES, AVX, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. It lacks AVX-512 extensions and dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within the middle tier for multi-threaded computation, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6224.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 13185.71. Software compilation using Clang scored 10890.0, and static web serving throughput reached 10.59 GB/sec. However, single-core processing throughput is limited by the older generation CPU architecture, showing weak comparative results in stress-ng single-core (1178.59), Geekbench single-core (980.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (20.19 GB/sec). Read-only large-block memory bandwidth is 82.56 GB/sec, while write operations reach 43.64 GB/sec.

Storage requires network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes, as m4.4xlarge contains no local instance storage. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance delivers solid multi-core density and balanced memory capacity on mature infrastructure, though its lower single-thread performance and limited network throughput reflect its legacy architecture.

This server profile fits moderate general-purpose workloads that can utilize parallel execution, such as application backends, mid-sized relational database hosting, containerized microservices, build nodes, and multi-threaded ETL jobs where heavy single-core clock speeds are not required.
description: Amazon Web Services m4.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.4 GHz. It features 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 64.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The instance lacks local storage, requiring network-attached volumes, and includes no GPU accelerators. Baseline network bandwidth is 2 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates average multi-core computing performance, logging a PassMark CPU score of 13185.71, a multi-core Geekbench score of 6224.0, and static web serving throughput of 10.59 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks register in the lower quartile due to the older architecture. With balanced compute and memory capacity, m4.4xlarge is suited for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, medium-scale databases, web application servers, and standard data processing pipelines.
